subject: BrightWave POC: inference playbook, candidate slate, and next steps
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: BrightWave POC: quick post-call recap

Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and immediate asks from our side so we keep momentum: 

- Goal we heard: reduce handoff friction on customer support workflows and generate concise, actionable summaries from multi-turn conversations with attachments preserved.
- Key constraints: 2s p95 latency target for single-turn summary requests, monthly token budget ~12M, and strict PII redaction requirements.
- Next asks from BrightWave: a short candidate slate (cost/latency/quality tradeoffs), a handful of prompt examples and a reproducible eval harness, and a proposal for a 4-week pilot.

I've attached the prompt pack we captured live (brightwave_prompt_pack_v1.txt). Ben & Marissa — can you review the slate below and confirm the commercial path (discounts / sandbox capacity) we can offer?

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@brightwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 16:31:00 -0800
Subject: BrightWave POC: candidate inference playbook + rationale

Alex / Priya — following up with the candidate playbook we recommend for evaluation. I've prioritized three configurations that balance your latency and budget targets with quality needs. Short take first, details below.

Candidate slate (recommended order):
1) redwood-1.3x-pro (FP16) — baseline recommendation
   - Why: Best end-to-end tradeoff for multi-turn summarization at our target sequence lengths; consistent semantic quality on our summary evals.
   - Cost estimate: ~0.035 USD per 1k tokens (generation + context).
   - Latency: ~1.6s p95 (single inference, 2048 context, continuous KV cache enabled).
   - Risk: Higher GPU footprint; minor rollout ops for quantization.

2) rw-econ-q4v2 (4-bit quantized) — cost-optimized variant
   - Why: ~40% lower per-token cost; still maintains strong factuality in our doc-summary tests.
   - Cost estimate: ~0.022 USD per 1k tokens.
   - Latency: ~1.9s p95 (some additional decode overhead, but within your 2s SLO in most regions).
   - Risk: Slightly higher hallucination score on zero-shot long-document prompts; we recommend prompt engineering + eval-guardrails.

3) open-hyper-13b-q8 (community model, q8) — fallback for constrained budgets
   - Why: Lowest infrastructure cost and easier licensing; reasonable baseline for early-stage pilots.
   - Cost estimate: ~0.015 USD per 1k tokens.
   - Latency: ~2.3s p95 (may exceed your SLO for heavy-context cases).
   - Risk: Noticeable drop in extractive accuracy; not recommended for final production without additional reranking or post-filtering.

Benchmarks and artifacts:
- Eval harness (per-example metrics) and raw run: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqBwBrightWaveEval (See folder: bw_bench_reports_20271121.pdf)
- Prompt pack used for scoring: attached (brightwave_prompt_pack_v1.txt).

Quality notes and regression guardrails:
- We ran prompt-level ROUGE / entailment checks plus a small human-rated factuality pass (n=120). Redwood-1.3x-pro outperformed others on factuality and instruction-following; rw-econ-q4v2 required a small prompt adjustment to reduce hallucinations (~4% improvement after adding an explicit grounding step).
- Recommended safety controls for pilot: deterministic prompt scaffolding, token-level PII redaction policy applied server-side, and a nightly regression job that runs the prompt pack against a held-out calibration set.

Operational asks to start pilot:
- Sign off on sandbox capacity (we can provision a 2-GPU sandbox cluster for 4 weeks).
- Access request: BrightWave engineer account(s) + test data ingestion (minimal PII subset).
- Commercial: trial credit note + optional one-time onboarding fee; Ben to propose numbers (Ben, can you provide a pricing sketch?).

Proposed timeline:
- Day 0–3: sandbox access + ingest sample data
- Week 1: run eval harness, collect failure modes
- Week 2–3: prompt tuning and latency tuning (batching/cache profiles)
- Week 4: decision checkpoint — production path (Dedicated / Hosted + SLA)

Let me know which candidate you want scoped first. If you'd like, we can start with rw-econ-q4v2 to validate cost benefits and then gate to redwood-1.3x-pro for production rollout.

Cheers,
Hannah

--
Attachments: brightwave_prompt_pack_v1.txt, bw_bench_reports_20271121.pdf
From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightWave POC: candidate inference playbook + rationale

Hannah — really helpful write-up, thanks. A couple quick follow-ups from our side: 

- Can you confirm the p95 numbers above are measured end-to-end (app request -> token stream complete) with the 2048 context and our typical attachment preprocessing?
- For rw-econ-q4v2, what was the hallucination failure mode? Is it primarily fabrication of dates/figures or omission of critical ticket metadata?
- Priya asked if we can have a small sample SWA (service-with-attachments) trace uploaded to the Drive folder so our infra can replay it against our edge proxy.

We're inclined to start the pilot with rw-econ-q4v2 to prove cost savings, but we want to validate latency in our environment before committing to the 4-week sandbox. Can we get the sandbox spun up early next week for a short latency smoke test? Also please include the HIPAA/PII handling checklist so our security folks can triage.

Thanks — Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightWave POC: candidate inference playbook + rationale

Alex — happy to run numbers and confirm the sandbox timeline. Quick answers: 

- Yes, p95 figures Hannah quoted are end-to-end measured on our hosted infra with a 2048 context window and the attachment preprocessor enabled (we normalize and chunk large attachments — that was included in the timing). We'll reproduce the same measurement in the sandbox for you.
- Hallucination failure mode on rw-econ-q4v2 was mostly omission + mild fabrication when prompts do not force grounding. Example: the model would omit an invoice line item in a summary or invent a delivery date when the source attachment had ambiguous date formatting. The mitigation we used: a two-step prompt (extract key facts -> synthesize summary) and a lightweight verification reranker. We included a snippet in bw_bench_reports_20271121.pdf.
- We'll upload a small service-with-attachments trace to the Drive folder by EOD and provision sandbox access early next week (target: Tue morning).

Commercial sketch for pilot:
- 4-week sandbox cluster (2x A10G equivalent) + evaluation support: $6,000 (one-time), includes 10k eval credits and 1 data-privacy review session.
- If BrightWave prefers a deeper Dedicated pilot we can price an interim Reserved bucket; Hannah/Marissa will follow-up on discounts.

Hannah/Marissa — can you prepare the HIPAA/PII checklist (server-side redaction, KMS notes, audit log retention) and a short how-to guide on turning on the nightly regression job? I can attach the commercial sketch to the HubSpot deal once we align.

Ben
